chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning four men who drank and became intoxicated. Then some of them took up weapons against the others and they fought, so two were killed and two were wounded. He ordered regarding the two wounded that each one of them be flogged with eighty lashes, and he ruled that the blood-money of the two slain was upon the two wounded. He also ordered that the wounds of the two wounded be assessed and deducted from the blood-money; and if one of the two wounded dies, then nothing is due from any of the heirs of the two slain.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ: the legal heirs or representatives of the slain
key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: weaponry used in the violent confrontation
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: the fixed punishment of eighty lashes
key_terms.جِرَاحَةُ: the wound or injury whose value is legally assessed
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money compensation owed for unlawful killing
key_terms.قَضَى: he gave judgment or issued a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام when intoxicated men fought and some were killed or wounded?
ai.summary: This hadith records a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning a violent incident caused by intoxication. It addresses punishment for drinking, liability for homicide, and the deduction of wound-compensation from the blood-money, showing principles of legal accountability in shared criminal cases.
